## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the deceitful ascetic is identified as the dishonest monk in the present, the king as Ānanda, and the Bodhisatta chaplain as the Buddha [Fausböll 1887]. The text's opening verse begins with the incipit *Kharājinā jaṭilā paṅkadantā* [Fausböll 1887].

 DharmaNexus corroborates this relationship through Pali-internal text reuse, identifying a matching segment between Ja 487 (§0.4–4.4) and Ja 377 (§3.1–6.4) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records substantial textual overlap with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (volumes 3 and 4), as well as automatic cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, the Tibetan *aṣṭādaśapaṭalavistaravyākhyā*, and the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) [DharmaNexus].
